steps.message: The project lives inside an ignored directory of an outer repo, so `git diff` is empty. Here is the patch content directly:

## Summary

**The bug:** `FileActivity` (`app/src/main/java/io/lerk/lrkFM/activities/FileActivity.java`) renders the directory contents in a plain `ListView` (`fileListView`). Every reload path — `reloadCurrentDirectory()` → `loadPath()` → `loadDirectory()`/`loadArchive()` — constructs a **brand new** `FileArrayAdapter`/`ArchiveArrayAdapter` and calls `fileListView.setAdapter(...)`. Swapping in a fresh adapter resets `ListView`'s internal scroll state, so the list jumps back to position 0.

This fires on every context-menu action that marks a file for an operation (`ContextMenuUtil` copy/move/zip marks all call `activity.reloadCurrentDirectory()`), which is exactly the reproduction in the report. There was no scroll save/restore logic anywhere in the codebase — no `setSelection`, `getFirstVisiblePosition`, or `onSaveInstanceState`.

**The fix:** Added two helpers and wired them into both load methods.

- `saveScrollPosition()` captures the index of the first visible row plus that row's pixel offset from the top (minus list padding), so the position is restored *exactly* rather than snapping to a row boundary.
- `restoreScrollPosition(int[])` re-applies it via `setSelectionFromTop(index, top)`, both immediately and again in a `post(...)` runnable so it survives the layout pass triggered by the new adapter contents.

Two details worth calling out:

- **Navigation still scrolls to top.** The restore is guarded by `boolean reload = path.equals(currentDirectory)`, captured *before* `currentDirectory = path` is assigned. Entering a different folder is a genuine navigation and correctly starts at the top; only a reload of the same path preserves position.
- **Both list types covered.** The same treatment was applied to `loadArchive()`, so browsing inside zip archives behaves identically.

The helpers null-check `fileListView` and short-circuit when already at the top, and the failure branches (`NoAccessException`/`EmptyDirectoryException`) deliberately skip the restore since the list is hidden in those cases.

**Verification:** `./gradlew clean assembleDebug` → `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`. Note that this confirms compilation only; the scroll-preservation behavior itself is not covered by any automated test in this project and would need a device/emulator to confirm visually.

## Summary

**The bug:** `FileActivity` (`app/src/main/java/io/lerk/lrkFM/activities/FileActivity.java`) renders the directory contents in a plain `ListView` (`fileListView`). Every reload path — `reloadCurrentDirectory()` → `loadPath()` → `loadDirectory()`/`loadArchive()` — constructs a **brand new** `FileArrayAdapter`/`ArchiveArrayAdapter` and calls `fileListView.setAdapter(...)`. Swapping in a fresh adapter resets `ListView`'s internal scroll state, so the list jumps back to position 0.

This fires on every context-menu action that marks a file for an operation (`ContextMenuUtil` copy/move/zip marks all call `activity.reloadCurrentDirectory()`), which is exactly the reproduction in the report. There was no scroll save/restore logic anywhere in the codebase — no `setSelection`, `getFirstVisiblePosition`, or `onSaveInstanceState`.

**The fix:** Added two helpers and wired them into both load methods.

- `saveScrollPosition()` captures the index of the first visible row plus that row's pixel offset from the top (minus list padding), so the position is restored *exactly* rather than snapping to a row boundary.
- `restoreScrollPosition(int[])` re-applies it via `setSelectionFromTop(index, top)`, both immediately and again in a `post(...)` runnable so it survives the layout pass triggered by the new adapter contents.

Two details worth calling out:

- **Navigation still scrolls to top.** The restore is guarded by `boolean reload = path.equals(currentDirectory)`, captured *before* `currentDirectory = path` is assigned. Entering a different folder is a genuine navigation and correctly starts at the top; only a reload of the same path preserves position.
- **Both list types covered.** The same treatment was applied to `loadArchive()`, so browsing inside zip archives behaves identically.

The helpers null-check `fileListView` and short-circuit when already at the top, and the failure branches (`NoAccessException`/`EmptyDirectoryException`) deliberately skip the restore since the list is hidden in those cases.

**Verification:** `./gradlew clean assembleDebug` → `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`. Note that this confirms compilation only; the scroll-preservation behavior itself is not covered by any automated test in this project and would need a device/emulator to confirm visually.
